subject: Re: Using your labelling and menu studies
body:
Dear Eric,

Thanks again for saying yes to the OSF data, and sorry for the slow reply.

You asked what I'm doing and why. I'm building a model that can give an early read on how different groups of people in the UK might respond to something like a label or a menu change, before anyone tests it for real. It learns from real randomised experiments like yours, where we know exactly what people saw and what they did. Studies that include the actual images are the hardest to find, and your lab has run more of them than any other group I've found.

I know the files are a lot of work to dig out, so I've put what would help most first, and even the first one would be great:

1. The full menu screens for each arm of the price promotions study (fxc8q) and the Nutri-Score delivery app study (pek74). The protocols only show examples. I've copied Amy, as these are hers.
2. For the fast-food menu boards study (ajcr6): the menu-board screenshots for each arm, the wording on the order screen, and if possible the item-level choices (main, side, drink) and demographics.

Nothing derived from your data would be published or shared with anyone, and I'll credit your work.

Thanks,
Rich
